result.markdown:
For a separation involving a complex property settlement in Brisbane’s eastern suburbs and Bayside, I’d focus on firms with demonstrable experience in **high-value property division, business and trust structures, superannuation splitting, and binding financial agreements (BFAs)** — rather than relying on general divorce experience or online star ratings alone.

One important distinction: a BFA is not automatically the best way to finalise a settlement after separation. Depending on your circumstances, consent orders approved by the Federal Circuit and Family Court of Australia may be more suitable.

I’ve looked at current Brisbane family-law rankings, specialist profiles and firms serving Carindale, Wynnum and the surrounding areas. The following shortlist is based on publicly documented specialisation and professional recognition, not a claim that any firm has a verified success rate in comparable cases. ## 4\. Questions to ask at your first consultation

For a complex separation, I would ask each firm the same questions so you can compare the actual lawyers and costs.

- **Comparable cases\:** How many property settlements involving trusts, companies, multiple properties or disputed valuations has this solicitor handled recently?
- **BFAs\:** How often do they draft, review or challenge binding financial agreements, including agreements made after separation?
- **Strategy\:** Would they recommend negotiating, mediation, consent orders or a BFA in your circumstances, and why?
- **Financial disclosure\:** How will they investigate missing information, asset transfers, loans between family members or disputed ownership?
- **Costs\:** What is the initial retainer, hourly rate, likely total cost at each stage, and the point at which litigation becomes significantly more expensive?
- **Who does the work\:** Will a senior family-law specialist personally lead the matter, or will most work be delegated?

A BFA generally requires each party to receive independent legal advice and must satisfy strict statutory requirements. Ask the solicitor to explain the risks of a future challenge and whether consent orders would provide a more appropriate way to finalise the settlement. One other important point: if you have already separated, don't assume that an informal agreement or an unsigned draft protects your assets. Get advice before signing documents, transferring significant property or agreeing to a final distribution.

## 4\. Questions to ask at your first consultation

For a complex separation, I would ask each firm the same questions so you can compare the actual lawyers and costs.

- **Comparable cases\:** How many property settlements involving trusts, companies, multiple properties or disputed valuations has this solicitor handled recently?
- **BFAs\:** How often do they draft, review or challenge binding financial agreements, including agreements made after separation?
- **Strategy\:** Would they recommend negotiating, mediation, consent orders or a BFA in your circumstances, and why?
- **Financial disclosure\:** How will they investigate missing information, asset transfers, loans between family members or disputed ownership?
- **Costs\:** What is the initial retainer, hourly rate, likely total cost at each stage, and the point at which litigation becomes significantly more expensive?
- **Who does the work\:** Will a senior family-law specialist personally lead the matter, or will most work be delegated?

A BFA generally requires each party to receive independent legal advice and must satisfy strict statutory requirements. Ask the solicitor to explain the risks of a future challenge and whether consent orders would provide a more appropriate way to finalise the settlement. [www.skenelawyers.com](https://www.skenelawyers.com/property-settlement-lawyers-brisbane/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.parkerfamilylaw.com.au](https://www.parkerfamilylaw.com.au/StayingoutofCourt.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[hartleyfamilylaw.com.au](https://hartleyfamilylaw.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/Prenuptial-Agreement.Binding-Financial-Agreements-compressed.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

One other important point: if you have already separated, don't assume that an informal agreement or an unsigned draft protects your assets. Get advice before signing documents, transferring significant property or agreeing to a final distribution.

## 5\. Let’s narrow this to the firms best suited to your case

The best shortlist depends substantially on what makes the property settlement complex. For example, a family business or discretionary trust calls for a somewhat different skill set from a dispute over the family home and investment properties.

**What is the main source of complexity in your property pool?**

1\. What assets are involved?

Family home and ordinary savings

Multiple properties and mortgages

Companies, trusts or a family business

Superannuation, inheritance or overseas assets

Several of the above or a high-value asset pool

---

2\. Where are you in the separation process?

We are negotiating an agreement

Negotiations are difficult or contested

An existing BFA needs reviewing or challenging

I need urgent advice before signing or transferring assets

---

3\. What matters most when choosing a lawyer?

Strongest technical expertise

Practical, settlement-focused approach

Local access in Carindale or Wynnum

Cost certainty and value for money

[Refine my shortlist]

I can then focus the comparison on the lawyers most relevant to your asset structure and whether you need to negotiate a settlement, formalise one or prepare for a contested property case.
